reviews.text: We loved this place for its vibrancy and amazing range of things that people do in this famous place. People’s Park in Shanghai originated from the British-run Shanghai Race Club, which was a famous horse racing and gambling venue in the 19th century. After 1949, racing was banned and, by 1952, the site was transformed into People’s Park and People’s Square, repurposing it for public and political events. Spanning about 10 hectares, the park is bordered by key city roads and surrounded by major landmarks, including Park Hotel, Tomorrow Square, and several cultural institutions. Over the decades, it has played an important role in political demonstrations, notably in the 1980s, and now serves primarily as a civic green space for leisure activities such as tai chi, dancing, and social gatherings — reflecting broader urban park life in China. Interestingly it is very famous for its weekend “marriage market,” where parents and relatives pin handwritten profiles of unmarried children—age, height, education, job, and sometimes property status—on umbrellas or boards to seek potential spouses.

A local Shanghai friend of mine took me here for a walk around! The park and the gardens are beautiful, the weather today was stunning and it's the 1st time I've seen blue sky since coming up to China in 1999. On a weekend the park turns in to a Matchmakers Market, where people who are looking for a spouse hire agencies to represent them and have their profile laid out for potential suitors. It is quite bizarre! There are literary thousands of them profiles lining the walkways and footpaths around the park. I'm love seeing new things but this takes the cake

People’s Park offers a welcome pause in the middle of Shanghai’s intensity, opening up into a broad, breathable space framed by incredible city views. Standing among the greenery, you’re constantly aware of the contrast—glass towers rising beyond the treeline, yet softened by the park’s openness and scale. It’s one of those places where the city reveals itself most honestly, not as spectacle, but as lived environment. In autumn, the park is especially rewarding. The trees take on warm, muted tones, creating pockets of colour that feel almost painterly against the skyline. Walking through the paths, watching locals stroll, exercise, or simply sit and observe, there’s a quiet rhythm that makes you slow down without trying. People’s Park isn’t flashy, but it’s deeply pleasant—an understated reminder that even in a megacity, there’s still room for light, space, and seasonal beauty.

People’s Park (上海人民公园) is a lively, centrally located green space that blends nature, culture, and everyday Shanghai life. It’s clean, easy to access, and always interesting—especially on weekends when locals gather for activities like dancing or the famous “marriage market.” A vibrant spot that’s well worth a visit.

The Shanghai marriage market is a unique experience for Western foreigners. Chinese parents display boards with their children's qualifications written on them for others to see. While they typically do not speak English, you can take a look at the boards. However, it’s important not to linger or take photos of the boards, as Chinese parents generally do not appreciate that.
In any Chinese city, the People’s Park is a must visit. It has the best local vibe, calm, lively, and far less touristy. Love it!

Very aged and not well kept mini carnival rides. Shockingly, my son enjoyed. Rides required a stored credit card and each ride cost between $2-$4. Lots of locals take up the park raising funds for various things. They weren’t pushy, but definitely were a presence within some sections of park.

People’s Park, Shanghai Shanghai’s People’s Park is a vibrant urban oasis located in the heart of the city, near Nanjing Road. Originally built on the former site of a horse racing track in 1952, it is a popular spot for relaxation, cultural activities, and social interactions. The park features lush gardens, scenic pathways, and tranquil ponds, providing a peaceful retreat from the bustling city. One of the park’s most unique attractions is the "Marriage Market," held every weekend. Parents gather to find suitable matches for their children, displaying personal details on handwritten sheets. This traditional practice draws locals and tourists alike, offering a glimpse into Chinese culture. People’s Park also houses the Shanghai Museum of Contemporary Art and various restaurants and tea houses. Its central location and cultural significance make it a must-visit destination, offering a blend of history, nature, and local traditions in the dynamic city of Shanghai.

This is a nice and large in the city center that provide visitors a place of serenity and tranquility from the busy and noisy traffic. There are lots of nice flowers and large greenery throughout the park where one can temporarily indulge in our mother's nature and enjoy peacefulness. It's a very nicely decorated park with colourful flowers and plants. There's also eatery, cafe and a flower shop there. However, during our visit, the weather was super sunny and warm and so there wasn't many visitors and even if there were, most were taking cover under the shade of tress or in the cafes. As the park is located near our hotel, we did pass by it everyday several times and enjoyed our walk there especially in the early morning. It's quiet and air was fresh.

Lovely park to escape the bustling city and enjoy some nature, lake views and sunshine. On the weekends people flock to the park as there are lists of bachelors and bachelorettes. It’s an in person tinder. You’ll mostly see the parents there shopping for their child’s soulmate. Definitely a site to see how China’s Matchmaking works

A nice park just across from the History Museum to have a little stroll avoiding the hustle and bustle of the city - you can look at the ‘CV’s’ that parents have left practically advertising their child to find them a partner, it’s a very interesting tradition to view. The park itself is well cared for with a nice koi pond as well.

A pretty park, but the main attraction here is the ‘marriage market’. Parents have the details of their sons/daughters written on sheets of paper or cardboard and engage in conversations with people (mostly other parents) to - potentially - make a deal. Truly unique and actually interesting to witness the scene.

Beautiful park in the city center of Shanghai. Even though it is between big avenues, once inside peacefulness comes. A favorite among locals and easily accessible with metro line 1, 2, and 8. On Saturdays you can see the marriage market, where (mostly) parents advertise their kids for marriage.

Not much to do here and very quiet. But it works well as a tranquil retreat! There are people playing games on the tables, there’s MOCA (art museum), an underground mall (south bit), but mostly just trees and paths to stroll in. A lot of seating which is nice. It’s takes a while to get round from the south to north bit due to lack of crossing points. Would recommend on a sunny day and on the weekend there’s the marriage market. But as a tourist wouldn’t go out of my way to visit this during winter.

People’s Square Park in Shanghai has always intrigued me, but what truly inspired my visit was the song 我在人民广场吃炸鸡 (“I’m Eating Fried Chicken in People’s Square”) by the songwriter 阿肆 (A Si). The melancholic yet catchy tune paints a vivid picture of urban loneliness, set against the backdrop of this iconic square. I wanted to experience the place that inspired such lyrics and explore its connection to the song. I was unable to find the fried chicken stall though. =)) I arrived around 7 PM and noticed a few people walking and jogging along the paths. . its immense size still struck me. It’s vast, with plenty of serene corners and shaded pathways that invite quiet reflection. For anyone familiar with 我在人民广场吃炸鸡, visiting this park feels like stepping into the heart of the song. It’s where the city’s hustle meets rare moments of peace—a memorable and meaningful experience.
We have been very impressed with the amount of and quality of green spaces in Shanghai. People’s square is another example. Well maintained environment for all to enjoy. Not crowded

Shanghai's People's Park offers a lovely green space for relaxation. Take a walk under the trees, enjoy the pond, or have a picnic. On weekends, a section becomes a marriage market. It's interesting to see families showcasing profiles of their single children in hopes of finding a match. This cultural tradition offers a glimpse into how some families approach finding partners for their children. Whether you're seeking peace or cultural immersion, the People's Park is worth a visit.

This garden is really well kept with the flower displays and hedges all in pristine condition. Like everywhere else there’s zero litter and plenty of benches give every opportunity to use it as a space to relax. It’s a large space with plenty of quieter sections too so if you’re looking for a central place without the crowds then consider escaping here. It’s easy to forget you’re in the middle of such a vast city but the towering skyscrapers surrounding serve as an impressive reminder. I really liked the park and would suggest adding it to any itinerary, even if only briefly.

I spent a quiet afternoon in People’s Park after exploring Nanjing Road, enjoying the change of pace. You can see locals chatting, older couples playing cards, and all nearby to the Museum. I found a spot near the fountain to people-watch and to watch thr fountain show. Beneath the park is an underground shopping centre with an arcade, worth visiting to escape the heat or enjoy some fun. It’s filled with shops, cafés, and games, contrasting with the peaceful greenery above.

The People's Park is also known as the Renmin Park, with a total area of 98,200 square meters (24.3 acres). It runs from Middle Xizang Road in the east to North Huangpi Road in the west, and extends from West Nanjing Road in the north to People's Square in the south. The park has eight gates; the main gate is located at no. 231 on the West Nanjing Road. The park can be divided into three areas: the east area, the middle area and the west area. The major attraction in the east area is the Memorial to the May Thirtieth Movement. The Antarctic Stone, the Shanghai Museum of Contemporary Art, a teahouse, an outdoor theater, and a dance hall can be found in the vast middle area. Additionally, tourists can have a rest, play chess, or have a picnic on the stone tables and stone stools in the jungle of the middle area. Compared with the east and middle areas, the west part has a lot of landscape architecture, including pavilions, corridors, artificial hills, pools and pergolas.

This is a beautiful and lively park. Arrive early in the morning to stroll in peace while the locals exercise and play cards. It is also a great place to begin your Shanghai touring with two excellent museums. The urban planning museum is focused on Shanghai’s past and future while of the china museum is focused on Chinese history. The museums open at 9 AM which is another reason to come to the park in the morning and go to the museums ahead of the crowds. The parks central location sets you up for a nice walking tour in any direction but if you’re not up for walking many bus tours leave from this area. It is also situated on top of a large metro station.

It’s Shanghai’s answer to NYC’s Central Park😎😎😎. It’s at the heart of the bustling mega-city. Strolling or just sitting on a corner of it is surprisingly blocked off the traffic noise. The green environment is very calming. The many benches just allows one to rest one’s weary legs from all the walking, and “sponge in” the coolish breeze to expel one’s sweat soaked shirt from the humidity.
Vibes, very peaceful and super clean, just like most of Shanghai. Nice walking paths been made, small ponds, kids area, little fair ground, lots of benches, nicely located

Nice garden in the hart of Shanghai with several museums around. In the north side and nearby Historical museum you can take a sightseeing tourist bus. 3 different lines are available. 100 rmb fir the whole day.

This isn’t the largest green space in a major city but, nevertheless, it’s really important for its inhabitants and visitors alike. Loved seeing locals exercising in the mornings and evenings; also loved the pond with the beautiful lotus flowers. The weekend was a revelation to us, with the ‘Marriage Market’; where parents seek a partner for their offspring! Adverts are either posted on boards by professional matchmakers or are simply attached to umbrellas to attract attention. In terms of content, the adverts here are the inverse of a Tinder profile; pictures and names are scarce, but salary and home ownership status are stated outright. That juxtaposition reflects traditional Chinese conceptions of marriage, in which weddings aren’t the culmination of a romantic courtship, but instead mark the beginning of an economic partnership whose main goal is producing children and sustaining a household. Fascinating - come rain or shine, every Saturday & Sunday between noon and 5pm. Great for people watching, but please don’t take pictures of the adverts themselves as that’s disrespectful.
Nice place at the center of the city. Huge park. Mix of both nature and concrete jungle.
A huge beautiful and clean public park. Can just buy a cup of coffee, and chill and people watching here for a few hours.

this park is centered in the heart of shanghai and is easily reached by many metro lines. In the spring time, you can discover many plants blossoming and blooming while exploring the beautiful flora it serves. On a sunny day you’ll catch many people picknicking or basking in the beautiful shanghai sun. As you submerge yourself into this landscape you are surrounded by many locals enjoying their day. It is a great opportunity to escape from the busy roads or the packed metro. Personally, one of my favorite places to be in shanghai. You could spend an entire afternoon there without getting bored. Plus, you won’t end up starving since there are many family marts or even restaurants close by.
It is beautiful, definitely worth visiting, it has a part with white doves which simbolizes peace
Beautiful park, except you enjoy sitting at the park enjoying the nature, nothing much in here.
If you love antiques you will love this place. Some room is free, some room got Fee.

A famous place where matchmaking occurs. Parents come out here with umbrella with profile of their children hanging and try to find the life partner for their children. There are whole bunch of umbrellas, and profiles are all in Chinese, so it would be an even more interesting experience if you can read them. Other than looking at the profiles, you can't really call this a park.

Definitely a pretty park, but ultimately I found it kinda uninspiring. Everything is very obviously man made with little to none of the wild aspects that Ive found to be so beautiful in most other parks in cities across China. I walked around for about 5-10 minutes and then I got bored.
Beautiful public space. Lovely to see older people dancing together with such joy and no inhibitions..a delightfully uplifting experience

For me it is beautiful. Especially in the morning were lots of Chinese are practising TaiChi/ChiKung/other excercises). On Saturday morning there's a very interesting event. Some kind of blink date, however I couldn't understand much because lack of knowledge of Chinese (photo attached).

This is a public park. Clean and safe. Great for a strawl. No barbecue facilities (I think that is not really big in China - this is meant to serve the local community and not some smug toursit), but there are restaurents around the place.
Beautiful Park, close to museum. A must see! I happened to go during National week.

1. Crowded, esp. weekends 2. Eager parents/ grandparents come across the country [maybe] and gather on weekends for matchmaking, truly one of the kind! 3. Umbrellas everywhere highlighting their son/ daughter qualities 4. House museums, exhibition halls, etc. 5. Meeting points, close to at least 3 metro lines, Line 2, 8 & 10 if I can remember correctly. 6. It is always bustling with activities, e.g. morning tai-chi, singing at night 7. Oh, it is free, for the park [not museum]

There's a matchmaking corner within People's Park where anxious parents put their children's information on display and even more anxious parents walk around looking for prospective in-laws. The park itself is incredibly ordinary though.

People's Square or People's Park in Shanghai. Nanjing Road. The Shanghai Art Museum and The Shanghai Grand Theater are located at people's park. Designed with manicured grassland and flowers. This multi-faceted park are surrounded by structurally designed old and new buildings.
In the weekends this park turns into a lively place where local people demonstrate sports, music, dance... Not to mis if you want to see some local spontaneous activity

reviews.text: What a nice park to walk around and getting fresh air. I don't know if that is because it was weekend or maybe it was too early, but no cafe inside the park was open today. It was very nice and well maintained park. We tried to visit one place which was sure if that were a cafe or restaurant but the staff was not very nice when he answered to us if cafe opened or not. Other then that, in general, don't miss visiting the park if you have some spare time
relaxing area to walk like this city would visit again but stay closer to the bund more high end shops and a little more relaxing

Among all of the parks in Shanghai, this is definitely one of them. There are so many vastly different sections it is like being in 20 different parks as you walk through and around it. Everyone raves about the flowers - and for good reason. But the grass and ground for picnickers is spectacular, particularly considering the concrete jungle surrounding it. The history of this area is amazing, and the racetrack outline is still vaguely visible on a map in the park layout on the north and Wu Sheng Rd. to the south. Accessing the historic club building of the Shanghai Race Club and its magnificent view of the area is challenging but worth it. .

great place to go for an amazing view, underneaththe park,there is an underground mall for people who love anime, lolita, ancient chinese fashion and lots more cute and fun stuff to buy and look at. the mall can be entered through the subway and although the first few stores maybe up for renovation, the best part of the mall is deep within the park itself!

Beautiful people populated open oasis of green and museums in the center of Shanghai. Come for a walk or to sit or to visit the nearby museum. On Sundays...you will find a colorful, unusual, bustling marriage market! People's Square (aka People's Park) is alive with people who have colorful umbrellas festooned with photos and biographical info on their sons and daughters in hopes of finding them the perfect match! I've travelled around the globe and have never seen anything like it. Be mindful that not all want their pix taken so be respectful and enjoy!
Pleasant place away from the hustle and bustle of central Shanghai. On Sunday morning you can catch a look at the parents trying to find partners for their adult children.

Beautiful park with many different areas to practice dancing or tai chi. It also includes water areas and in the middle of one of them there's a beautiful historic tea house where you can have tea ceremony, including quail eggs.

Expansive park, multiple egress points. I had heard about the famous Shanghai matchmaking events and was interested in seeing it up close, but alas I was unable to align the timing of my park visit. An easy stroll to view the lush and well maintained greenery of the multiple scenery. Placards with both Mandarin and English descriptions.

Ren square is really good place to sit and chill in a heart of the big city of Shanghai. Love that place, want to visit it on more time. +Clean +Has a lot of benches and nice atmosphere +In the middle of the city +Probably you can do some good pictures here

The famous "matchmaking" area for people to try get their kids married. Don't be surprised - it is common and always happens in this park. People will post salary, height, age, and other information of their children and try to match make them. Just go to the southern park of the park where there are no such people and enjoy the peace.
It's a great park for a wander around. The metro station is huge with exits all over the park. The Shanghai Museum is right there, too.

It's a nice little park, with a beautiful small lake that makes you forget of the traffic all around it. You are sure to pass from here if you are a tourist, don't hesitate to take a small 20 minutes break.

A nice place to have a rest if you feel tired in the downtown Shanghai. A lot of funs here. You can see the local residents playing cards, chess, dance. Moreover, you can find a unique dating corner here. Many parents help their kids to find Mr. Right or Miss Right here by exchange photos and information. Very interesting! For more details about Shanghai, twitter me@jerryshanghai.
Nice place for a walk and bring the kids. Not far from shopping mall and the bund so can do lots of things nearby
Nice quiet walk.. ended up later at Barbarossa bar... Nice... Good luck finding it...

Large expanse of green land with inner lakes and streams. Popular with locals and tourists as well. Famous for both the spontaneous English corner in the past and nowadays the bride-and-bridegroom wanted corner. Free entry.
Super quiet for a park located centrally in shanghai. Great to visit if you need some space from bussloads of tourists. Used to be a horse racing course apparently!

People park is the center of Shanghai, sourrounded by the sky scrapers and beautiful park. Its the center of metro station where u canswirch to any lines. It's in the proximity of the Huang Pu river and the Bund. There are many restaurant l, street food stall and shops. Its amazing and well managed place. It ie the most dense place of Shanghai but you will not feel the crowd. Its a muat visit place in China 🇨🇳.

reviews.text: Well maintained and frequented by people. A breath of fresh air in the middle of a great metropolis. Nice benches for the elderlies. Free toilet facilities. Clean too.

FIVE STARS BECAUSE SHANGHAI ABSOLUTELY NEEDS FOR OF THESE GREEN SPACES People's Park stands out a small oasis of greenery in the frenetic, crowded downtown Shanghai. You won't be alone in the park, but it does give some respite from the masses surging along the nearby streets!
Beautiful park! If you see a lot of people with umbrellas and signs, it is a lover's market where parents try to hook their children up with other parents' children.
Awesome place to walk around and admire the views and the people. It was cold when I was there during winter but this made me want to return in the summer and I definitely shall.
Lovely green surrounding in the middle of one of the biggest cities in the world. I enjoyed all the plants, flowers, fountain...Lovely athmosphere
A green park, and a nice pedestrian shopping/walking street. Very popular, so not the best place if you are looking for reasonably priced local style food restaurants.
Beautiful park in Shanghai where you can even take a nap like the locals do, or have a picnic, it is really well maintained and during weekends very crowded with locals enjoying the free time
Marriage market: noon-5pm sat and sun is a spectacle. Almost (but not really) worth a visit just for it, but swing by if you're at nanjing Road or something in the vicinity.
Beautiful urban park that functions as a haven of relaxation among the hustle and bustle of the People's Square area of the city.
It is a park, but for first timers, lookout for escalators going downwards, that is where it will bring you to a whole new underground shopping centre
Well kept and lush green urban park in the middle of the city. I am assuming this is public space but there is awfully a lot of people smoking in spite of no smoking sign everywhere.

Nice park aside from all the roads and buildings, lake in the middle and people playing games, could have been larger tho!
Good foor visiting daytime on weekends when there is this real life tinder going on!
Nice little park, close to the Shanghai museum. There are cherry blossoms in the spring.
Not a great park, but a decent greenish area in the middle of a very urban city.
It was interesting to see the weekly marriage marked, hosted by parents that are looking for a spouse for there grown kids
Come to the marriage market on Saturday and Sunday. Great for walking around and people watching.
Great place for people watching. Go see flawless exercises by people from all walks of life.
It was a very rainy day the day I went so there was no one about or as busy as it usually is.

完全に大都会上海の中心にあるOASISです。園内はめっちゃ広くて散歩にはうってつけです🖖私が行った時にまず目に入ったのが、「婚活のプロフィールを掲げた数々の人」です。しかもご本人でなくおそらくご両親の方々が活動されてます。ちょっと私の祖国では馴染みがなくてビックリしましたが、新な出会いが生まれるかもつ思うと素敵な行動ですね、ただしその様子を写真撮ろうとすると滅茶苦茶怒られるので注意です！！ 池やお話、遊戯や小規模な遊園地もあったのでなかなか飽きることはないかなって思います、また行きたいのだﾆｷ！

上海人民公園位於市中心的南京西路旁，是鬧區中少數仍保有大片綠地的地方。與台灣多數開放式公園不同，這裡依然保有外牆與明確的出入口，需由指定的門進出。 園內植被茂密、綠意盎然，步道兩側的樹蔭讓人能稍微遠離都市的喧囂。不過園中也能看見老舊的兒童樂園與一些已停用的設施。 最具特色的是著名的「相親角」，許多長輩會在此張貼子女的資料、交換條件，為孩子尋覓理想的對象。 不過園內仍有部分遊客抽煙，略微影響整體體驗。 整體而言，人民公園是個觀察上海城市生活與人文縮影的地方。
晚上六點多來到這個人民公園，結果有點意外，在路上看到好多隻野貓？而且公園的燈光非常昏暗。！這真的不像一個堂堂上海的人民公園？在公園裡非常昏暗，人潮也很少。這對公園來講其實是很負面的，沒有散步運動的民眾。而且混亂的地方容易造成社會犯罪的角落？對這公園真的是蠻怪異的？很少大陸公園會有這種情況發生？？
Bardzo duży park w centrum Shanghaju ,z jednej strony znajduje się Muzeum Shanghajskie bezpłatne warto zajrzeć i podziwiać ,brązy, kaligrafię czy jadeity itp.,

Il parco è facilmente raggiungibile in metro ed è abbastanza grande, pulito e ben curato. Dispone di diverse panchine dove sedersi e rilassarsi. È un luogo ideale per trascorrere qualche ora in tranquillità immersi nel verde.
Nel parco e nel week end le persone con gli annunci per sposarsi o condividere gli ultimi anni assieme, anche come badanti
（2024/9/9） 與地鐵人民廣場站接壤，周邊有上海城市規劃展示館、上海市歷史博物館、上海當代藝術館、上海博物館等，離南京路步行街也挺近。不錯的散步地點，在周六周日來似乎還有相親角。

Un parque muy muy bien cuidado , frondoso . Todo verde y siempre tienen gente limpiando tanto baños como los paseos de adoquines . Nosotros fuimos entre semana y después de que cayera un poco de agua en agosto y estaba muy tranquilo y con olor a hierba mojada . Tienen cafeterías y restaurante dentro , baños públicos y una zona de parque de atracciones para los más pequeños . La verdad que es un lujo el poder pasear entre medio de los árboles , ver los nenúfares y sacarte unas bonitas fotos . Recomendado 💯. Después si quieres volver a la civilización sales y te encuentras com la calle dirección bund, y parada de metro línea 1

人民公園位於上海黃浦區的核心地帶，不僅是上海地鐵交通樞紐，在地理位置上也接近市中心。一旁便是繁華的南京東路步行街，這條街匯聚了百年老字號品牌店、國際時尚精品店以及各類餐飲，成為遊客來上海必訪的購物與觀光勝地。除了商業價值外，人民公園還因「相親角」而聞名。每逢週末，公園一角便擠滿了替子女或親友尋找婚姻對象的家長與媒人。他們手持子女的基本資料，如年齡、學歷、工作、收入等，並相互交流，希望為子女物色一個合適的伴侶。然而，這種相親方式往往過於重視經濟條件與社會地位，而忽略了雙方的性格、興趣愛好與價值觀是否契合，甚至讓人覺得更像是一場婚姻交易。儘管如此，相親角依舊是上海一種獨特的社會現象，除反映了傳統與現代價值觀的碰撞，也展現了父母對子女婚姻的深切關心。對於遊客而言，這裡不僅是一個觀察當地文化的好地方，也能讓人對上海乃至中國的婚戀觀有更深入的了解。
Lieu plaisant sans la chaleur du mois d’août . Magnifique et agréable tranquillité assuré et des fleurs extraordinaires de couleurs dans le mini parc aquatique

People's Square (Plac Ludowy) w Szanghaju to jedno z najważniejszych miejsc w tym dynamicznym mieście. Znajduje się w centrum, otoczone ważnymi budynkami, takimi jak Muzeum Sztuk Pięknych, Teatr Narodowy oraz ratusz. Jednym z największych atutów tego miejsca jest jego przestronność. Plac jest idealnym miejscem do spacerów i odpoczynku po intensywnym zwiedzaniu miasta. Zieleń i starannie zaplanowane przestrzenie sprawiają, że jest to prawdziwa oaza w tętniącym życiem mieście. Można tu dojechać metrem, a także busami, co czyni go doskonałą bazą wypadową do zwiedzania. Jest to miejsce, które zdecydowanie warto odwiedzić.
На выходных многолюдно. Красиво, в конце пешеходной улицы выходишь к набережной, где можно увидеть восточную жемчужину и небоскребы. Хорошие локации для фото.
인민광장은 사람들이 많을것같지만 안많아요 릴리안베이커리랑 하이디라오랑 상하이에서 한끼해결 할 식당들이 즐비해 있으니 한번은 와서 길 걸으면서 상하이 바이브를 즐기는것도 나쁘지않을겁니다
생각보단 작고 아쉬운 공원 규모 ^^ 아침 운동겸 갔는데 큰 입구만 열려 있고 작은 출입구들은 다 막혀 있었어요.조깅 트랙은 나쁘진 않았지만 노인 분들이 많이 이용하는 공원 느낌.

Ein schön angelegter Park und eine tolle Möglichkeit, dem Trubel der Metropole Shanghai für eine Weile zu entfliehen und ein wenig auszuspannen 😌 Landschaftlich schön angelegt, sehr gepflegt und mit vielen Sitzgelegenheiten ausgestattet ✔️
Spokój na trochę oddechu w centrum Szanghaju. Wejście tylko przez wyznaczone bramy, bo całość ogrodzona. Cisza i spokój na łonie przyrody. My byliśmy wiosną.

上海を代表する公園の１つです。上海中心部の中では最も大きな公園だと思います。そもそも中心部には緑が少ないので貴重な緑地です。中には、池があり、簡単な遊園地がありといった様子であり、平日土日ともに多くの人がいます。ここの名物なのがお見合いイベントです。両親が自分の子供の恋人を探すイベントであり、子供の情報（学歴、身長、年齢、年収など）を書いた紙を広告として傘に貼って宣伝しています。世界的にも取り上げられてるので一度見てみて下さいくださ！

上海 人民公園名物の傘お見合い。傘に娘や息子の履歴を書いて貼ってます。おじさんおばさんがお互いの履歴書を見ながら何やら話をしています。 太極拳をしているおじさんに、ムチを振ってるおじさん、青空で麻雀しているおじさんや何か変な楽器弾いてる人とかも居ます。 美術館やお洒落なレストランバーBarbarossaも有ります。 人民広場に住んでた時は、よく散歩してました。近くに無料の上海博物館も有るし、楽器店街も有るし、足を伸ばせば外灘まで行けるし、結構気に入ってました。 上海の政治の中心なので、みんな何でそんな所に住むのって言われたけど、結構気に入ってました。日本人も少ないし。

פארק יפיפה עם המון פינות שקטות לשבת בהן. אווירה רגועה של טבע ושלןוה ממש במרכז העיר עצמה, מרחק דקות הליכה מרחובות השופינג ההומים. בימי ראשון אחהצ יש מפגש שידוכים של המקומיים וזו חוויה מדהימה, מאות אנשים עם שלטים בהם פרטי הילדים/נכדים שלהם מוצעים לשידוך.
假日充滿父母或媒婆的相親角 為各種需求或條件的男女找另一半 非常狀觀、精彩，甚至還有國外角 很推薦抱著健康的心態看一下不同社會狀況形成的文化 個人覺得來上海必來的點
Cuối tuần thứ 7 nhưng công viên cũng khá đông, mọi người đi lại tắm nắng bên hồ. Lá đổi màu nhiều rồi đó.
Hermosa plaza Aquí se puede visitar la tumba de Mao, la entrada es gratis, pero se agotan rápidamente Cadi diría que es más linda visitarka x la noche
Piazza centrale è molto conosciuta a Shanghai, una macchia di verde ed un bel punto di ritrovo .. il traffico intorno è terribile, vicinissima ad una delle passeggiate principiali.
Тихое место в центре города. Можно посидеть и отдохнуть. Или посмотреть на растения . Полюбоваться озером. А так же погладить кошку.

비오는데도 운치있어여 공원끝쪽에 스타벅스있는데 창가자리좋으나 밖에서 보이는 유리창영역이 다일만큼 직사각구조로작음 비추천 화장실없음 공원은 난징동루서 일자로걸어오믄되고 이층투어버스가 대부분여기이ㅣ 티켓샵있어요 난징동루서 길건너서 일자로가시면 티켓박스 지하철인민광장역 찾기쉬워요 공항 가거나올때 이용쉽게 눈에팍띄는데 단드가믄 엄청크고복잡한역이니 목적지 가는곳 타는곳번호를 미리찾아놓으신후 내려가셔오ㅡ 입구에서 짐검사있음 현금없이도 위챗페이로 티켓구매가능 인터넷에 사는법있음

Eine grüne Lunge unweit von der berühmten Fußgängerzone "Nanjing Road" und umgeben von einigen Hochhäusern, mit einem Restaurant, einem Ausstellungspavilion und einem kleinen Kindervergnügungspark. Im Park treffen sich insbesondere ältere Leute zum Sport, Spielen und zum Vermitteln von Heiratskandidaten für die eigenen, noch unverherateten Kinder. Ein aus der Südpol-Expedition mitgebrachte Stein ist auch aufgestellt.

Un très beau parc au cœur de Shanghai. Très agréable sans doute pour ceux qui ont besoin de voir un peu de verdure, mais aussi très agréable a parcourir. Le parc lui même mais aussi tous ce qu'il y dedans, le grand théâtre ou le musée de Shanghai. Et comme c'est la plaque tournante du métro de Shanghai ça permet de faire une aide agréable.
Excelente la Plaza del Pueblo. Genial armado de la fuente y el show con luces y chorros de agua acompañando la música.

En el centro de Shanghái, bien comunicado con tres líneas de metro para llegar fácilmente a cualquier punto de interés. Lleno de comercios. Los domingos , muy curioso pasear viendo el mercado de los hijos solteros,anunciados por los padres mediante anuncios en los paraguas.
Um parque muito bem cuidado como todos em Shanghai. Esse particularmente é muito frequentado pelos moradores locais expondo um pouco dos hábitos e cultura local

C est parc entouré d immeubles et pas loin pour démarrer la promenade dans la rue nanjing grande rue commerçante qui vous amènera au bund. Le week-end en tous cas surprenant le marché du mariage avec des affichettes que je vous invite à traduire avec un descriptif des femmes à marier en chine passer 30 ans c est mal vu de ne pas être marié

Localizado em uma das regiões mais centrais da cidade. Seus 30 acres de canteiros de flores, lagoas e árvores servem como quintal para milhões de moradores que vivem nos arredores. É um local onde moradores e turistas se reúnem para apreciar a mistura de arquitetura histórica e moderna, desfrutar de eventos culturais e explorar a vibrante vida urbana da cidade. Aos finais de semana o parque vira palco de uma das atrações mais bizarras de Xangai: a “Feira do casamento”. Do meio-dia às cinco da tarde, pais desesperados de filhos solteirões se reúnem em busca de parceiros para seus rebentos.

Großer, gut angelegter Park mit vielen Bereichen in der Nähe der Nanjing Road. Das Shanghai Museum und das Theater sowieso das Gebäude der Regionalregierung sind dort ebenfalls zu finden. Samstags ist in einem Bereich immer Hochzeitsmarkt.

Dejlig hyggelig park med et ældre, lidt slidt tivoli til de yngste børn. Stille og roligt område hvor unge og gamle hygger sig med spil, fysiske øvelser, gåture og samtaler. Marts måned er lidt for tidligt i forhold til blomster.
Für mich der schönste Park den Shanghai zu bieten hat mit seinen Seerosen und Lotus. Am Wochenende ist es sehr voll. In der Woche ist angenehm ruhig. Der Park ist gut mit der U Bahn zu erreichen.

上海へ訪れたらとにかく週末に一回は訪れてみたい公園です。週末になると上海のお父さんやお母さんが自分たちの息子、娘達のためにお見合い相手を探しに出てきます。「これは一体なんなんだ！」って思わず不思議で仕方なくなってしまいますが、ここで本当に子供の結婚相手を探しているのです。朝から昼過ぎくらいまでが一番多くの人がいると思うので、その時間帯に行ってみては如何でしょうか。社会学の論文にできそうな光景ですよ。

公園自体はとても良い場所ですが、ここではボッタクリに誘う詐欺グループがいたので注意です（学生風、男女グループ）。ティーフェスティバルに行こうと言われますが行ってはいけません。同行すると雑居ビルの茶館に連れて行かれお茶を飲み、会計の時に女性の分おごってあげようよって言われてかなり高めのお金を払わされます。そのあと別の店（カラオケ？）に誘われましたがそこで断ったためその後はわかりません。
２日続けて訪れました。 常にどこかで音楽が響いていて、一人旅の自分としては、この賑やかさに癒されました。 また、あちこちでおじさんが盤ゲームをやっていて、その周りにもおじさん見物衆が集い、ああだこうだと興じていました。 日本も一昔前まではこうだったのかなと思うと、少しむなしさがありますね。

Increíble lugar. Un espacio cuidado en su diseño y bien mantenido, con espacios diferenciados y aprovechado al máximo por los habitantes para realizar todo tipo de esparcimiento al aire libre. Un oasis de verde y tranquilidad en medio de una jungla de cemento.

ぽんちゃんです。 以前 上海に赴任していました。 上海旅行ではここははずせませんよね。とっとノウハウを(笑) 時々 休日に行った公園です。 見方のポイントは、早朝に行くことです。 太極拳をしている人など中国っぽい雰囲気がいっぱいです 是非 行ってみてくださいね 追伸 中国の人は日本人を感覚で見分けているようです 呼び込みに引っかからないコツは日本語を会話しないことです。中国語で会話していると声がかかりにくいようです。日本語で会話していて近づいてきた人がいましたが、中国語を話した瞬間 戻って行ったことがありました(あくまでも私見ですが 笑)

Gemütlicher, belebter und volksnäher als der "Volksplatz" auf der anderen Seite des Regierungsgebäudes. Hier gibt es zahlreiche Spaziergänger und v.a. sonntags den mittlerweile auch in den Medien diskutierten Heiratsmarkt der Einkind-Eltern, die mit beachtlichen Geboten heiratswillige Frauen für ihren männlichen Nachwuchs suchen.Warum es derer mehr gibt, d. h. was seinerzeit mit den weiblichen Babies (und etwaigen Zweitkindern) geschah, wird natürlich weder hier noch anderswo im Land, wie z.B. auf Youtube, thematisiert.

جدای از طبیعت و فضای سبز بسیار زیبای این پارک جیزی که توجه من رو بیشتر از همه به خودش جلب کرد وجود یه سری بنگاههای دوست یابی وسط پارک بود. به این ترتیب که پدر مادرها عکسهای پسر یا دخترشون رو با اطلاعاتشون میارن تا براشون همسر پیدا کنن. یه سری اقراد هم لیستی بلند بالا دارن تا از این طریق به دیگران کمک کنند. وقتی علت رو جویا شدم فهمیدم متاسفانه انقدر اینجا سرشون شلوغ میشه که افراد فرصت دوستیابی ندارند اغلب. پارک واقعا فوق العاده بود.
